endpoints.description:
PANSS Total Score is a clinician administered measure of schizophrenia symptom severity used widely in antipsychotic research. It includes 30 items across 3 subscales:

  • Positive Symptoms (7 items) assessing excesses or distortions such as hallucinations, delusions, or grandiosity
  • Negative Symptoms (7 items) assessing diminished function such as social withdrawal or reduced motivation and
  • General Psychopathology (16 items) capturing broader symptoms like anxiety, depression, guilt, or cognitive impairment Each item is scored from 1 (absent) to 7 (extreme), producing a PANSS Total Score ranging from 30 to 210, with higher scores indicating more severe symptoms.

Baseline is defined as the last non missing PANSS Total Score before first dose.

This endpoint evaluates change from Baseline to Week 6, with negative values indicating improvement.
endpoints.measure: Change From Baseline in Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) Total Score at Week 6

analysis_trace: Trial NCT05145413 is a Phase 3 study of KarXT (xanomeline-trospium) as adjunctive therapy for inadequately controlled schizophrenia symptoms. The primary endpoint is change in PANSS total score at Week 6. Retrieved literature includes Phase 2 (EMERGENT-1) and Phase 3 (EMERGENT-2) trials showing significant PANSS improvements. EMERGENT-2 (published 2022) demonstrated -9.6 point difference vs placebo (95% CI: -13.4, -5.7) for PANSS total change at Week 5. EMERGENT-3 and EMERGENT-4 trials reported similar efficacy. The mechanism involves M1/M4 muscarinic receptor agonism without direct dopamine blockade. Safety profile shows cholinergic side effects (nausea, vomiting) but no extrapyramidal symptoms or weight gain typical of antipsychotics.

Evidence assessment: EMERGENT-2 (direct_numeric) - same drug, same indication, similar population, PANSS total endpoint at Week 5 (close to Week 6). Effect size ~9-10 points. Numeric use allowed with timepoint adjustment. EMERGENT-3/4 (indirect_direction) - confirmatory Phase 3 trials with consistent results. KarXT received FDA approval September 2024, supporting efficacy.

Endpoint-specific analysis: Primary PANSS total (primary-0): Based on EMERGENT-2 (-9.6 points at Week 5) and consistent Phase 3 results, predict ~-8 to -10 point change for active vs ~-2 to -3 for placebo, difference ~6-7 points. CGI-S (secondary-2): Correlates with PANSS; expect ~0.3-0.4 point improvement. Categorical response (secondary-5): Based on EMERGENT-2 30% response rate ~40% vs 20% placebo, expect ~35-45% active vs 15-25% placebo.

PSP (secondary-1), PANSS Marder factors (secondary-3, secondary-4), and POM (secondary-6): These endpoints have endpoint_type='not_evaluable' in contract, indicating the contract does not support prediction for these specific endpoints.

Key uncertainties: Exact Week 6 vs Week 5 timing, adjunctive vs monotherapy population differences, and specific categorical response thresholds. Confidence moderate-high for primary and evaluable secondary endpoints based on consistent Phase 3 evidence.
